sentences.text: This animal is known only from a partial skull found in Barremian-age rocks of the Vectis Formation on the Isle of Wight.
Its short and wide skull features a eusuchian-like palate and enlarged posterior teeth adapted for crushing.
Hylaeochampsa is currently recognized as the oldest known unambiguous eusuchian.
Richard Owen described the genus in 1874, naming Hylaeochampsa vectiana as the type species.
Researchers James Clark and Mark Norell classified Hylaeochampsa as the sister group to Crocodylia.
The animal lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, approximately 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago.
